items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the penal law, in relation to expanding the crime of making graffiti
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5218

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the penal law, in relation to expanding the crime of
making graffiti

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 145.60 of the penal law, as added by chapter 458 of the laws
of 1992 is amended.

Section 145.60 (1): defines making graffiti in the second degree in
this section and in section 145.62 of this article.

Section 145.62: expands definition of making graffiti in the first
degree

 JUSTIFICATION :

Graffiti is not a victimless crime. No matter what form it takes,
defacing public or private property damages such property and someone
must pay for the clean-up of such damage. Whether a homeowner,
corporation, small business owner or taxpayer, there is a cost
associated with graffiti removal and this cost can be substantial.

A person is guilty of making graffiti in the second degree when he or
she etches, paints, covers, draws upon or otherwise places a mark upon
public or private property with intent to damage such property.

A person is guilty of making graffiti in the first degree when such
person damages property of another person in the same manner as
described in section 145.60 if within the previous ten year period,
such person has been convicted and sentenced for the crime of any of
the following: criminal mischief in the fourth degree on three or more
occasions, criminal mischief in the third degree, criminal mischief in
the second degree, or criminal mischief in the first degree as defined
by section 145.62 of this article and damages property of another
person in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars.

The a-print of this bill changes the title of the bill and aligns the
language of making graffiti with that of criminal mischief.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

Previously introduced

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first November next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law

summary: Expands the crime of making graffiti.
